body.statement:
There is a strictly positive even unit-norm function \(\psi\).  If \(h=-2\psi'/\psi\), then for some finite constant \(M\),
\[
h(x)^2-2h'(x)=|x|-C_A,\qquad
|h(x)|\le M(1+\sqrt{|x|}),\qquad
|h'(x)|\le \frac{M}{1+\sqrt{|x|}},
\]
and both \(h^2\) and \(h'\) are globally Lipschitz.

source.locator: The Airy feedback proposition in the proof section for the second-order risk theorem of arXiv:2608.13822v1, together with the immediately preceding Airy ground-state proposition
source.verbatim_statement: \(h_A(t)^2-2h_A'(t)-|t|=-C_A\), \(|h_A(t)|\le K(1+\sqrt{|t|})\), \(|h_A'(t)|\le K/(1+\sqrt{|t|})\), and \(h_A^2,h_A'\) are globally Lipschitz continuous.

attestation.note: Transcribed from the Airy feedback proposition in arXiv:2608.13822v1; positivity and the eigenfunction equation were checked in the preceding proposition.
